title: National ACS household vehicle scarcity and long commute exposure changed modestly across 2023–2024
source_unit: ACS 1-year national table estimates: B08201 household vehicle access and B08303 travel time to work

denominator.unit: B08201 national households for vehicle measure; B08303 workers 16+ not working from home for commute measure

commute_30_minutes_or_more.unit: percent of workers not working from home

observations.method: Direct national rows from ACS 1-year table-based summary files. Commute 30+ combines B08303 categories 30-34 through 90+ minutes. No person matching or cross-year causal estimate.
observations.uncertainty: ACS sampling and nonsampling error apply; no margin-of-error propagation is calculated in this first national layer. The commute universe excludes people who worked from home and is not the same as NHTS recorded trips.
observations.subgroup: All US households for vehicle access; workers 16 years and over who did not work from home for commute time.
observations.counterinterpretation: A small national change can hide large state, income, race, disability, and urban/rural differences; vehicle availability and commute duration do not establish affordability, necessity, or unmet care access.

denominator.unit: B08201 national households for vehicle measure; B08303 workers 16+ not working from home for commute measure

commute_30_minutes_or_more.unit: percent of workers not working from home

observations.method: Direct national rows from ACS 1-year table-based summary files. Commute 30+ combines B08303 categories 30-34 through 90+ minutes. No person matching or cross-year causal estimate.
observations.uncertainty: ACS sampling and nonsampling error apply; no margin-of-error propagation is calculated in this first national layer. The commute universe excludes people who worked from home and is not the same as NHTS recorded trips.
observations.subgroup: All US households for vehicle access; workers 16 years and over who did not work from home for commute time.
observations.counterinterpretation: The modest national movement does not validate the NHTS urban/rural or income gradients by itself; separate geographic and socioeconomic ACS tables are required for that test.

boundary: This is an annual national ACS household/worker comparison, not a longitudinal respondent panel and not a direct replication of NHTS. B08201 measures household vehicle availability; B08303 measures commute time among workers who did not work from home. The current record does not establish household income gradients, care/medical reachability, trip purpose, fares, or political/cultural response. The next test is a state or place/income ACS extension with margin-of-error handling and explicit comparison to NHTS's urban/rural and travel-day universes.
